title: RevokeAccessFlow
wrapsNative: MonarchBottomSheet (dismissible = false keeps it open while revoking) with androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column, MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchTypeToConfirmInput, MonarchInlineNotice, MonarchButton and MonarchStepUpAuthDialog; android.text.format.DateUtils for the last-used time
summary: A recipe, not a component: confirm revoking an API key, an OAuth client, portal access, sessions or devices, listing what is revoked, when it was last used and what happens, with optional type-to-confirm and re-authentication.
whenToUse: Behind every Revoke, Sign out or Remove action on keys, connected apps, sessions, devices or someone's portal access.
whenNotToUse: For a simple sign-out of one session, a MonarchDialog (ConfirmDialog) is enough. For deleting a whole workspace, use the same pattern with the workspace's own wording.
api: MonarchBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { confirming = false }, title = "Revoke “$keyName”?", description = …, dismissible = !revoking) { … }
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(phrase = keyName, value = typed, onValueChange = { typed = it })

MonarchButton(text = "Revoke key", onClick = …, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Danger, enabled = MonarchTypeToConfirmInputDefaults.matches(typed, keyName), loading = revoking)
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog(onVerify = …, description = "Revoking access needs you to confirm it’s you.", onVerified = …)

options.name: keyName
options.description: The name of what is revoked, written in the title and typed to confirm.

options.name: lastUsedMillis
options.description: When it was last used, in epoch milliseconds; null reads "Never used".

options.name: typeToConfirm
options.default: true for keys and OAuth clients
options.description: Whether the danger button waits for the name to be typed exactly.

options.name: needsStepUp
options.description: Whether the server requires a recent confirmation; the sheet then shows MonarchStepUpAuthDialog and revokes after it verifies.

options.name: revoking
options.description: The request is running: the danger button shows its progress indicator, Cancel is disabled and the sheet cannot be dismissed.

options.name: failure
options.description: A failed request, shown in a danger MonarchInlineNotice in the sheet.

states.name: confirm
states.description: The question naming what is revoked, a line on what it means, the item with its prefix and last-used time, the consequence list, and the danger and Cancel buttons.

states.name: type to confirm
states.description: For keys and OAuth clients, the danger button stays disabled until the name is typed exactly.

states.name: step-up
states.description: When re-authentication is required, the sheet shows MonarchStepUpAuthDialog; the revocation runs after it verifies.

states.name: revoking
states.description: The danger button shows its progress indicator; Cancel is disabled and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice in the sheet; the person can try again.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component on the sheet's surface: a heading, body text, the consequence list with its marks, the type-to-confirm field and full-width danger and ghost buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's RevokeAccessFlow is one component with built-in copy for five kinds (api-key, oauth-client, portal-access, session, device) and plural forms. On Android, as on iOS, it is a recipe: the copy is the app's, written for its kind and count, and the step is a MonarchBottomSheet because a MonarchDialog cannot comfortably hold a list, a text field with a match check and a pending state. Danger is right for keys and OAuth clients, which cannot be undone; for sessions, devices and portal access, which can sign in again, use a plain MonarchDialog or the same sheet with warning wording. The web's stepUp prop is MonarchStepUpAuthDialog shown in the same sheet. The last-used time is written with DateUtils.getRelativeTimeSpanString (minSdk 24, no java.time).
accessibility: The title has the heading semantics.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed name matches.
The row's Revoke button is named with the item ("Revoke CI deploy key").
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 48dp targets and a loading state while revoking; the sheet cannot be dismissed while revoking, so the result is not lost.
edgeCases: For several items, list each one and put the count in the title and the button ("Revoke 3 keys").
An item never used reads "Never used" instead of a time.
Reset the typed name each time the sheet opens.
After a failure keep the sheet open with the typed name, so the person can try again.
